outputs.L4:
An LED device includes a substrate and a plurality of LED units mounted on the substrate. Each LED unit may include one or more light-emitting elements and corresponding electrical terminals. The LED units are electrically coupled by conductive structures arranged along opposing sidewalls of the substrate, thereby providing power and signal paths between the LED units and any associated external circuitry.

A first group of conductive structures is disposed on a first sidewall of the substrate, while a second group of conductive structures is disposed on a second, opposing sidewall. The first and second groups contain unequal numbers of conductive structures, allowing the two sides of the LED device to support different terminal arrangements or electrical connection configurations. For example, one side may provide a greater number of individually addressable connections, whereas the opposite side may provide shared power, ground, or common signal connections.

Each conductive structure includes a middle portion and first and second extending portions extending from respective ends of the middle portion. The extending portions have different lengths and may extend onto adjacent surfaces of the substrate, such as its upper and lower surfaces. The longer extending portion may electrically connect to a corresponding LED unit or substrate-mounted conductive trace, while the shorter extending portion may form an external contact, inter-unit connection, or mounting interface. The relative lengths and orientations of the extending portions can be selected according to the required routing and connection arrangement.

Through this asymmetric interconnection design, the conductive structures electrically connect the plurality of LED units while permitting distinct electrical configurations on the opposing sides of the device. The arrangement may reduce routing complexity, support compact packaging, and facilitate installation or connection of the LED device within a larger lighting module, display, or electronic assembly.
outputs.L5:
## LED Technology

LED stands for **light-emitting diode**, a semiconductor device that produces light when an electric current passes through it. LEDs are widely used in homes, offices, vehicles, electronic displays, streetlights, and industrial equipment.

One of the main advantages of LED lighting is energy efficiency. LEDs use significantly less electricity than traditional incandescent bulbs while producing a similar level of brightness. They also have a much longer lifespan, which reduces replacement and maintenance costs.

LEDs are available in many colors, shapes, and brightness levels. Modern LED products can include features such as dimming, motion detection, color adjustment, and smart-home connectivity. Unlike conventional bulbs, LEDs generate relatively little heat and reach full brightness almost instantly.

Because of their durability, versatility, and low energy consumption, LED solutions have become an important part of sustainable lighting. Choosing LED lighting can help lower electricity bills, reduce waste, and create flexible illumination for both indoor and outdoor spaces.

a substrate;  
a plurality of LED units disposed on the substrate, each LED unit comprising an LED structure having a first sidewall and a second sidewall opposite the first sidewall; and
